fields.sample_size: 20 Brazilian municipalities with the most confirmed COVID-19 cases compared with the 20 most populous and the 20 with the worst sanitation indicators (SNIS, IBGE, Instituto Trata Brasil 2020 data)
fields.effect_estimate: Municipalities with the most COVID-19 cases overlap with those with the worst water and sewage indicators (case-count municipalities are 50% Northeast and 25% North by region; worst-sanitation municipalities 40% North). SDG 6 attainment is low: 45% for 6.1, 25% for 6.2/6.3 and 0% for 6.4. The authors discuss the role of regulation (regulatory agencies) but describe lack of services as a factor that hinders prevention, not a cause. Descriptive cross-referencing of rankings; no statistical test.
fields.study_design: documentary cross-referencing of national indicator rankings (SNIS) with COVID-19 case counts by municipality
fields.section: Full text: Metodologia; Resultados (Table of regional distribution; SDG 6 attainment); Discussao (role of regulation)
fields.exact_location: Metodologia; Resultados (Table of regional distribution; SDG 6 attainment); Discussao (role of regulation)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a descriptive cross-referencing of SNIS water and sanitation indicators with COVID-19 case counts in the top-20 Brazilian municipalities, read in full text 2026-10-04. Overlap between high case counts and worst indicators; SDG 6 attainment 45%/25%/0%; regulation discussed. No inferential statistics.
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the 20-municipality design and regional shares. Ecological ranking comparison, no test.
